correctness.rationale: PASS: Independent Bernoulli benchmark and n-agent allocation quantifiers are explicit; benchmark is not claimed to be a uniform random allocation marginal when p≠1/n. Convolution Z_t+Y with Y∼Bin(n,p) gives exact F_{t+1}−F_t. For k<=t, a_{k−1}/a_k <=(1-p)/(p(n−1)), yielding lower bound a_t(1-p)^n(1−H_n(p/(1-p))); H_n(1/(n−1))=1 and H_n is coefficientwise increasing. Thus all subcritical tails >=F_1=(1-p)^{n−1}, with n=2,p=1/2 equality. The cited matroid-intersection reduction bounds m−|A0|<=n(k+1−v(A0))−1; Barman–Verma MMS allocation simultaneously attains benchmark. Uniform rank-one matroids on n−1 goods are sharp below and at threshold; uniform rank-t on nt−1 goods has p>1/n left-tail→0 as t→∞, proving zero uniform guarantee (not zero for every fixed instance). Independently compared 759 exact rational binomial monotonicity samples, not used to certify theorem for all n,t,p.

value.rationale: PASS: Gives exact critical p=1/n value conjectured in the 2023/2024 quantile-share primary paper and an all-subcritical/supercritical phase diagram on the natural matroid-rank domain, with sharp cutoff from positive level to zero when arbitrarily many goods are allowed. The n-agent Bernoulli benchmark is mathematically motivated and the exact classification is more than a routine numerical or feasibility check.

limitations: Newer specialized comparisons might give the exact subcritical tail inequality or full matroid phase without using quantile-share language. The standalone critical binomial inequality is closely related to mode monotonicity and is not claimed independent of that theory. Above threshold zero guarantee is uniform over unbounded m, not a claim that every finite instance has zero feasible probability.
